Public Comment: The public is encouraged to address City Council on any matter listed on the agenda or on any other matter
within its jurisdiction subject to the rules of decorum described in Section 2.08.020 of the Norwalk Municipal Code. If you wish to
address City Council, please complete a speaker card and hand the card to the Sergeant at Arms. City Council will hear public
comment on items listed on the agenda during discussion of the matter and prior to a vote and on matters not listed on the
agenda during the Oral Communications period.

Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless certain
emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for
consideration at a future City Council meeting.

Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the City Council: Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less
and
directed to the City Council as a whole and not directed to individual Councilmembers.

Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City meeting or
other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk’s department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening devices are
available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and documents in the
agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability. Notification of at least 48
hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring that reasonable arrangements
can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it has
been posted will also be made available for public inspection. Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City
Clerk’s Department, during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday – Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every
other Friday; telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e-mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

Gov. Code § 84308: Parties to any proceeding involving a license, permit, or other entitlement for use pending before the City
Council must disclose any campaign contribution over $250 (aggregated) within the preceding 12 months made by the party, their
agent, and those required to be aggregated with their contributions under Gov. Code § 82015.5. The disclosure must include the
amount contributed and the name(s) of the contributor(s). "G.C. § 84308: Yes" on this agenda indicates that the item is subject to

  REGULAR MEETING

Mayor Rios called the meeting to order at 6:04 p.m. in the Council Chambers, Norwalk
City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard, Norwalk, California. Responding to roll call were
Councilmembers Perez and Valencia, and Mayor Rios. Vice Mayor Ayala arrived after
roll call; Councilmember Ramirez was absent. Also present were Jesus M. Gomez, City
Manager; Gloria V. Ramirez, Deputy City Attorney; and Theresa Devoy, City Clerk.

The invocation was delivered by April Reutter, Pray Norwalk; followed by the flag salute,
led by Young Marine Sergeant Estrada, LCpl Kenneth L. Worley Young Marines.

CITY COUNCIL COMMENTS

Councilmember Valencia reported on her attendance at the Teen Alliance Program (TAP)
awards ceremony, the Padres Unidos gathering, the California Contract Cities
Association (CCCA) conference, congratulated Councilmember Perez on being elected
President of the CCCA, thanked Allan Perdomo, Director of Recreation and Park Services
and staff for their outstanding work at the CCCA conference, reported that City Manager
Jesus Gomez will be leading the CCCA City Managers, commended Recreation and Park
Services staff for their Teen Alliance Program presentation at the CCCA conference;
attended the Leadership and Advocacy for the Direction of Young Women (L.A.D.Y.)
program event, the Norwalk Memorial Day event at City Hall, and wished all the fathers
a happy Father’s Day. Councilmember Perez commented on Memorial Day, reported on
her installation as the new CCCA President, thanked staff for their work planning and
working the CCCA conference, shared an update on Senate Bill 1383 and reminded
everyone that as of January 1, 2024, fines have been going into effect as per the
provisions outlined in the bill, a presentation by TAP which highlighted its overwhelming
success; reported on a commitment from former Norwalk Councilmember Marcel Rodarte
for an annual scholarship for TAP and a donation from Los Angeles County Supervisor
Janice Hahn; she attended the International Council of Shopping Centers (ICSC)
conference where she met with business owners and shared insight and goals for
Norwalk. Vice Mayor Ayala reported on his attendance at Santa Fe High School band
concert, mentioning the joint performance by the California, Whittier, and Santa Fe High
School bands; congratulated scholarship recipients from Soroptimist International, and
thanked everyone that attended the Little Lake City Educational Foundation Golf
Tournament. Mayor Rios welcomed everyone in attendance, reminded everyone of the
Norwalk 5K Run/Walk on June 2 and the Pray Norwalk event at the Double Tree Hotel
on June 1; reported that she was invited to be a keynote speaker at the California State
University Long Beach “Gear Up” program event, attended the Mujeres Extraodinarias
Foundation “Mente Sana, Vida Plena” event at Cerritos College, the Norwalk Memorial

met with developers, brokers and potential Norwalk tenants.

City Council recognized Norwalk High School Student Artists for designing and painting

City Council presented a proclamation declaring May 19 – May 25, 2024 as National

SUBJECT:  2024 APPLICATIONS FOR RETAIL FIREWORKS SALES PERMITS

Background:

Each year the City receives applications for retail fireworks sales permits. Norwalk Municipal
Code Section 5.36 authorizes up to 20 qualified organizations to sell safe and sane fireworks
between July 1 and July 4 annually.

An orientation meeting with representatives from the applicant organizations and each
wholesaler was held on March 20, 2024. Twenty organizations attended this meeting and
received presentations made by staff from the Finance and Public Safety departments. These
presentations outlined the rules, regulations and proper safety procedures for fireworks stands.
The orientation meeting was mandatory and considered part of the application process.

The deadline for submitting an application requesting the fireworks sales permit was May 1,
2024. Of the 20 organizations that attended the orientation meeting, 17 submitted an application.
Once received, applications were reviewed and qualified based on the process and qualifications
previously approved by City Council. The remaining three organizations, which were Norwalk
Pony Baseball, Lansang Jiu Jitsu, and Friends of Norwalk Youth, did not submit an application.

As the number of qualified applications for retail fireworks permits did not exceed 20, a random
drawing was not required. The organizations listed on the following page are being
recommended to receive a retail fireworks sales permit.

SUBJECT:  PROJECT NO. 7927.2 - ACCEPTANCE OF WORK FOR - LOCAL STREETS
  REHABILITATION PROGRAM ZONE 3 – ENGINEERS REPORT 24-09

Background:

On June 16, 2023, staff solicited for construction bids for the Measure M Bond funded City
Project No. 7927.2 - Local Streets Rehabilitation Phase 2 roadway surface improvements. The
project area is located within City Pavement Management Zone 3, bounded by I-5 freeway to
the east; Imperial Highway and Firestone Boulevard to the south; and the Union Pacific Rail
Road line to the west as shown on the attached map. R. J. Noble Company was selected as the
contractor for this project.

The project scope improved roadway surface conditions through multiple rehabilitation methods
consisting of grind and overlay, specific location full-depth removal/replacement, and slurry seal
coating. All pavement markings (striping, legends, crosswalks, etc.) have been restored
following paving operations. Crosswalks were upgraded to current continental standard where
applicable for enhanced pedestrian safety.

The project was completed satisfactorily on May 29, 2024.

Fiscal Impact:

The project was funded using $5,804,242 of Measure M funds that were included in the Fiscal
Year 2023/24 budget. No General Fund monies were used for the project. Unexpended funds
in the amount of $406,224 are available for reprogramming.

SUBJECT:  AGREEMENT – CAPITAL BUS TIRE LEASING SERVICES FOR NORWALK
  TRANSIT SYSTEM

Background:

On February 1, 2024, the City issued a Request for Proposal (RFP) No. 24-736 for Bus Tire
Leasing Services for Norwalk Transit System (NTS). Two proposals were received from the
following vendors: (1) The Goodyear Tire and Rubber Company (Goodyear); and
(2) Bridgestone Americas Tire Operations, LLC (Bridgestone). Each firm’s proposal was
evaluated in keeping with RFP requirement criteria including, qualifications, experience, detailed
work plan & schedule, proposed project team, organization, price, and completeness of RFP
documents:

  Firm  Total Score
 1  The Goodyear Tire & Rubber Co,  96%
 2  Bridgestone Americas Tire Operations, LLC  73%

NTS staff reviewed the proposals and determined Goodyear was the most responsive and
responsible proposal based on their extensive experience, qualifications, technical capacity, and
resources to provide the required services. As the current incumbent, Goodyear has made a
commitment to ensure that all services and tires continue to meet or exceed federal and state
requirements; and that safety and fleet availability is not compromised.
 City Council  June 18, 2024
Agreement – Capital Bus Tire Leasing Services  Page No. 2

Fiscal Impact:

Funding for the first year of the capital lease agreement, in the amount of $88,000, is included
in the adopted Fiscal Year 2024/25 Transportation Department budget. There is no impact to
the City’s general fund as the Capital Tire Lease Program is funded by the Federal Transit
Administration Section 5307 Grant funds for 80% of the cost and the remaining 20% is funded
with Proposition A Local Return funds.

   SCOPE OF SERVICES

1.  Overview. The City of Norwalk, Norwalk Transit System (NTS) is seeking proposals from
qualified and experience firms to provide bus tire leasing services for NTS’ heavy-duty bus fleet.
Contractor shall provide all new tires, re-groove and re-retread (rears only), labor, tools,
equipment that are in good working condition necessary to mount tires on wheels, dismount tires
from wheels, and perform necessary repairs to tires such as flats, air tires, and tire balance.
Contractor shall perform services described herein on a weekly basis on the entire active bus fleet
on City premises located at 12650 E. Imperial Hwy., Norwalk, CA 90650.

1.  General Requirements. Proposer must have five years experience providing bus tire
  leasing services to a public transportation agency. Proposers must be either the Original
  Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) or an authorized dealer of the types of tires described
  herein.

3.  Hours of Operation. Contractor shall provide services between 5:30am to 10:30pm on
Saturday and/or Sunday. Contractor shall provide a minimum of eight (8) hours of service weekly.

4.  Holidays. The below table is the City’s holiday schedule. Contractor is not obligated to
work on Contractor’s observed holidays.

  Non-Observed Holiday  Observed Holiday
  Martin Luther King Jr. Day  New Years Day
  President’s Day  Memorial Day
  Veteran’s Day  Independence Day
  Labor Day
  Thanksgiving
  Christmas

5.  Accidents/Incidents. Contractor shall notify the City immediately if City property and/or
Contractor's personnel and/or subcontractor personnel were involved in an accident or incident
in relation to the services provided by the Contractor and/or subcontractor. Contractor shall
provide the City a detailed written detailed description within three (3) business days of the event.

6.  Annual Mileage.  The mileage for Fiscal Year FY 2023 was 991,389 or 82,616 miles
per month. NTS reserves the right to add or reduce miles as needed without immediate notice to
the Contractor.

7.  Tires Furnished. All tires furnished by Contractor shall be of high quality, radial tire
design suitable for Transit operations. All materials used in the manufacture of the tires furnished
under this bid shall conform to all U.S. Government and State of California laws and regulations
and likewise the manufacturing of the tires furnished shall conform to all federal, state, and local
laws and regulations.

  7.1  Tires shall provide reliable transit bus service, free from excessive noise and
vibration, and free from defects in material and construction.

  7.2  Contractor (“Lessor”) shall provide tires meeting all applicable federal, state, and
local laws and regulations.
  EXHIBIT A
   7.3  Tires to be run on front wheels shall be new tires only and shall be removed when
the tread depth reach 5/32” minimum at any point in the tread configuration. Tires to be run on
other than front wheels shall be removed when depth reaches 3/32” minimum at any point in the
tread configuration.

  7.4  The use of re-grooved tires shall be limited to the rear axle of transit buses shall
comply with all federal, state, and local laws and regulations.

  7.5  All tires provided are to be factory molded and D.O.T approved for 65 mile per hour
city and suburban use. All tires shall be capable of 65MPH sustained operation.

  7.6  NTS shall not be precluded during the life of the contract from including in the
contract new or improved tires that may be developed by the Contractor. Contractor shall provide
tires that the NTS may add, at NTS’s sole discretion, to its fleet. The City and Contractor will
mutually agree on the specified new tire added as an amendment to the contractor signed by both
parties.

  7.7  Tires Unfit for Service. NTS will remove tires from service immediately when
determined unfit by either the Successful Contractor or NTS. Contractor’s tires are to be
removed from NTS property within 30 days of determination of unfitness, in accordance
with local, state and federal laws and regulations

8.  Inventory. Contractor shall monitor and control tire inventory and to ensure a number of
mounted spare tires for buses, so that City, at all times, will have a stock of tires to maintain
continuous operation of its buses. The amount of spare tires shall be mutually agreed upon
between City and Contractor. All spare tires shall be mounted on City provided wheels.

  8.1  Within two weeks after the effective Agreement date, Contractor shall inspect all
bus tires in NTS possession, shall record the tire numbers and provide NTS with a listing of all
tires, with appropriate comments on exceptional conditions encountered regarding fitness of tires
for continued use or need for changes.

  8.2  In the event of a manufacturing delay in tires due to a strike, the Contractor shall,
to the degree possible, prior to the effective day of the strike, ship additional spare tires sufficient
for NTS to maintain uninterrupted transit service during the manufacturing delay.

  8.3  In any event, it is the Contractor’s responsibility to assure an adequate supply of
tires at all times.

  8.4  The Contractor shall be responsible for controlling the tire purchasing process
through the entire contract period including option years in order to ensure that NTS has a
sufficient inventory of tires.

  8.5  Annual Inventory. At least once a year on a date to be agreed upon between
Contractor and Fleet Maintenance Manager or designee, Contractor will perform a physical
inventory of all leased tire stock on City property and provide the City with an electronic file
containing the inventory results.

  8.6  Tire Branding. Contractor shall brand all tires furnished to NTS individually or
group with their own unique identification number prior to delivery. Contractor shall accurately
list inventory on the Monthly Report.
  EXHIBIT A
   8.7  NTS will not transfer, sublet, or lend the tires furnished by, or permit the tires to
be used by, anyone other than NTS, or its agents, without the prior written consent of the
Contractor.

9.  Title of Tires. Ownership and title to any leased tires and equipment shall remain with
the Contractor unless and until a tire is purchased by NTS as provided for at the expiration of the
contract, expiration of the run-out period, or in a scrap tire contract.

11.  NTS’ Responsibilities.

  11.1 NTS will provide a secured space with its Equipment Maintenance Shop for tire
related equipment and space for tire inventory to be stored.

  11.2 NTS staff will provide mileage data on a per bus per month basis for the
purpose of billing for the service rate and tire mileage lease no later the 15 th of each
month.

  11.3 NTS will replace tire/wheel assemblies that are necessary to be done on
the road, noting that spare assemblies shall be provided to NTS via the Contractor for this
purpose.

  11.4 NTS will service tires as needed and to Original Equipment Manufacturer’s
recommendations in accordance with industry best practices.

  11.5 Fleet Maintenance Manager or designee will investigate misalignment and
other conditions reported by the Contractor and correct as necessary.

  11.6  NTS will provide necessary air and electrical outlets for tire service
equipment.

12.  Contractor Services. Contractor shall provide and maintain in a safe operating condition
all labor, equipment, tools and supplies in the provision of leased tires.

  12.1 Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM). Contractor and Contractor’s
subcontractor must meet or exceed Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) specification
standards and workmanship at all times.

  12.2 Contractor shall ensure that no bus is kept from next day revenue service due to
the Contractor’s failure to perform required tire services.

  12.3 Mounting / Dismounting. Contractor shall be responsible for mounting and
dismounting tires.

  12.4  Torquing.

  12.4.1 Contractor shall ensure all wheel nuts are properly torqued.

  12.4.2 Contractor shall safety stripe all wheel nuts after they are torqued.

  EXHIBIT A
   12.4.3 Should the torque wrench provided by Contractor be inoperable,
  Contractor shall hand torque all wheel nuts pursuant to the OEM
  specifications.

  12.4.4 Contractor’s torque wrench shall be maintained to OEM specifications and
  calibrated in accordance with OEM requirements. Contractor’s torque
  wrench shall possess a tag indicating certification.

  12.5  Balancing. Contractor shall balance all tires utilized in the front position only.

  12.6 Rotation. Contractor shall inspect tires to verify need for rotation. Contractor shall
rotate tires pursuant to the OEM specifications.

  12.7  Tire Repair. Contractor shall repair all tire punctures and flat tires.

  12.8 Tire Inspections. Contractor shall perform a weekly visual inspection of all tires for
tread depth, visual defects, adversities, or damage, including defective or leaking valves,
defective or loose valve stems, and missing valve caps. Contractor shall visually inspect tires for
evidence of irregular wear that may occur as a result of mechanical adversities. Tires determined
to not meet standards or possess defects, adversities, or damage shall be removed. Contractor
shall promptly notify City of such findings.

  12.9 Tire Pressures. Contractor shall perform weekly tire air pressure checks and
maintain OEM inflation specifications on buses. Contractor shall visual inspect alignment or
misalignment for each type of tire application and adjust tire pressure accordingly.

  12.10 At no time shall the Service Technician be authorized to drive the buses. City staff
will assist the Contractor to maneuver the buses as needed.

13.  Contractor Service Technician(s). At no time shall the City be without the services from
the Service Technician(s) provided by the Contractor. Necessary arrangements shall be made by
Contractor to provide continuous coverage when the Service Technician(s) is/are unavailable due
to scheduled or unscheduled time off. Contractor shall notify NTS immediately of such events.

  13.1 Service Technician(s), including all subcontractors, performing the services
described in the Scope of Work herein shall be properly trained with mounting and
dismounting tires and operating procedures regarding manual and machine methods in
accordance to OSHA 1910.177.

14.  Tire Delivery

  14.1 Delivery. Contractor shall obtain City written signature for acceptance of all tire

damage does not include heat-related cracking of the tire in and around the bead area and such

   17.3 Tires that are damaged beyond repair due to an accident or fire, vandalism, or

mileage remaining, less the mileage already paid for on the damaged tire. The remaining mileage
shall be prorated by determining the percentage of tread rubber remaining, multiplied by the
Expected Tread Life (Exhibit B) multiplied by the effective base rate per tire mile (Exhibit B). Value
shall be fixed for the term of the contract.

  17.4 When a tire is not available for inspection to apply the above formula due to loss,

SUBJECT:  AGREEMENT – SUPPLY OF AUTOMOTIVE PARTS AND SUPPLIES

Background:

On March 28, 2024, the City issued an Invitation for Bid (IFB) No. 24-737 for Supply and Delivery
of Automotive Parts and Supplies. The purpose of the IFB is to acquire Original Equipment
Manufacturer aftermarket, and remanufactured parts/supplies for City-Wide vehicles and
Norwalk Transit System (NTS) fleet.

NTS received four bids, from the following: 1) Cummins, Inc., 2) Elliot Auto Supply Co. Inc. 3)
H&H Auto Parts Wholesale, and 4) Parts Authority, LLC. Staff reviewed the bids and determined
that H&H Auto Parts Wholesale provided the lowest and most responsive/responsible bid.

Fiscal Impact:

NTS is seeking a three year contract, plus two one-year options for parts and supplies. The cost
for the first year of the contract totals $35,000 which is included in the Fiscal Year 2024/25
Transportation Department adopted budget. There is no impact to the general fund.

SUBJECT:  RESOLUTION NO. 24-28 - ADOPTING PURCHASING POLICY FOR FISCAL
  YEAR 2024/25

Background:

Annually, the City is required to update its Purchasing Policy in accordance with the Norwalk
Municipal Code (NMC) Chapter 3.16.

In order to provide effective administration of the purchasing ordinance (NMC Chapter 3.16), the
Purchasing Policy is updated on an annual basis. This update may include competitive bidding,
purchasing practices, related administrative authority, etc. One such change to be considered
each year is a change in the Purchase Authority authorization limit – the limit for which purchases
may be approved of by the Purchasing Authority (City Manager) without City Council approval,
as long as there is available funding in the Adopted Budget. In accordance with Section 3.16.060
of the NMC, the Purchasing Authority authorization limit is to be “automatically adjusted on
July 1, 2021 and each July 1st annually thereafter based upon the percentage change in the
Consumer Price Index (“CPI”) for the Los Angeles-Anaheim-Riverside area as published by the
U.S. Department of Labor from March of the prior year to March of the current year.”

The attached Purchasing Policy, Exhibit A to Resolution No. 24-28, reflects the annual update
to the Purchasing Policy for Fiscal Year (FY) 2024/25, effective July 1, 2024.

The Purchasing Policy for FY 2024/25 has the following changes:

  • Authorization Limits
  o Purchasing Authority (City Manager) authorization limit is established at $39,400. This
  represents an increase of 3.9% from the FY 2024 level of $37,900 and is based on

 CITY OF NORWALK POLICY STATEMENT

Number:  24-28
Subject:  Purchasing Policy
Adopted Date:  June 18, 2024
Effective Date:  July 1, 2024

BACKGROUND

The main theme of the Manual reflects the philosophy of the Finance Department to
obtain supplies, equipment, and services as required by all Departments in a timely
manner, at the best possible price, and within the boundaries as set forth by City policy.

PURPOSE

 To establish City policies and procedures regarding the purchasing ordinance of the
 City of Norwalk (NMC Chapter 3.16) — this includes competitive bidding, purchasing
 practices, and related administrative authority. The purpose of this policy is to provide
 for the effective administration of the purchasing ordinance. This system has been
 developed in order to achieve the following objectives:

  1. Secure goods and services at the lowest cost possible commensurate with
  quality requirements.

  2. Establish authority, responsibility and accountability for purchasing activities
  conducted on behalf of the City.

  3. Ensure competition and impartiality in all purchasing transactions to the maximum
  extent possible.

  4. Standardize procedures where appropriate to ensure that organization-wide
  policies and goals are achieved.

  5. Maintain Department responsibility, initiative and flexibility in evaluating, selecting
  and purchasing goods and services.

  6. Implement simple yet effective internal control procedures that appropriately
  support planning, maximize productive use of public funds and protect City assets
  from unauthorized use.

  7. Communicate organization-wide purchasing goals, policies and procedures to
  Departmental staff involved in purchasing activities.

 Application of Purchasing Policy

 The purchasing policy and procedures applies to the purchase of all goods (supplies,
 materials and equipment, and nonprofessional (NMC Chapter 3.16), professional
 services (NMC Chapter 3.21) and public projects (NMC Chapter 3.17).

  3

 Purchasing Authority designated - Powers and duties (NMC 3.16.050)

The City's purchasing ordinance delegates purchasing authority to the City Manager.
The Purchasing Authority may delegate all or a portion of the contracting or purchasing
duties to any City staff member. The Purchasing Authority’s functions shall include the
following powers and duties:

  A.  Negotiate, purchase, and contract for supplies, materials and equipment, and
  Services required by City Departments, within the authorization limits of 3.16.060,
  pursuant to the procedures provided in chapter 3.16;

  B.  Endeavor to obtain as full and open competition as possible on all purchases;

  C.  Supervise the inspection of all supplies, services, and equipment purchased to
  ensure conformance with specifications;

  D.  Develop, prescribe and maintain, such administrative policies, forms and files as
  may be reasonably necessary for the efficient purchases on behalf of the City;

  E.  Prepare procedural regulations governing the purchase of supplies, materials and
  equipment, and services, in accordance with the requirements prescribed in this
  chapter;

  F.  Facilitate the transfer of surplus or unused supplies and equipment among
  Departments as needed;

  G. Recommend the sale or disposal of all supplies and equipment which cannot be
  used by the City, or which have become unsuitable for City use;

  H.  Maintain a bidders’ list, vendors catalog file and records needed for the efficient
  operation of the purchasing Department

General Policy

General Purchases

Purchase of all supplies, materials and equipment, and nonprofessional services (NMC
Chapter 3.16), and professional services (NMC Chapter 3.21) will be made pursuant to
the following guidelines.

1. Over-the-Counter
  Purchases for less than $8,700 (exclusive of sales and use taxes) may be authorized
  by the Department Head. Although no specific purchasing requirements are
  established for this level of purchase, competitive bidding should be used whenever
  practical.

2. Informal Bidding/Open Market
  Purchases, with an estimated value over $8,700 and up to the Purchasing Authority
  Authorization Limit of $39,400 (exclusive of sales and use taxes) may be made in the
  open market through the City’s online bidding platform.

  a. Wherever possible, open market purchases must be based on at least three
  (3) informal bids, and must be awarded to the lowest responsible bidder. If the
  lowest quote is not selected, the Purchasing Authority or designee chall
  document in writing the basis for such election NMC Section 3.20.010.

  b. Informal bids must be conducted through the City’s online bidding platform.

  c. The Finance Department must view bids from prospective vendors prior to
  purchase.

3. Formal Bid
  Purchases with an estimated value greater than Purchasing Authority Authorization
  Limit of $39,400 (excluding sales and use taxes) must be obtained by the Formal Bid
  Procedure pursuant to NMC Section 3.20.020.

  a. The City Council approval is required when value is higher than the
  Purchasing Authority Authorization Limit.

  b. Formal bids must be conducted through the City’s online bidding platform.

Bidding – Exemptions – NMC 3.16.070

Preparation of the Bid Package - The initiating Department shall prepare the bid package

There are seven essential components to the Bid Package: Notice Inviting Bids, Bid
Terms and Conditions, Bid Security, Performance Bond, Bidder's List, Bid
Specifications, and Bid Submission form. The following is a description of each of these
components:

1. Preparing Notice Inviting Bids - The notice shall be prepared by the initiating

  d. Time and place for opening bids

  General Notice Inviting Bids - Notice Inviting Bids must be published at least 10 days
  before the date of bid opening on the City’s website. The Purchasing Authority, or
  designee, may also choose to publish the notice in a local newspaper, trade
  newspaper, or trade journal in order to provide notice to the largest number of
  prospective bidders.

  Advertising - The initiating Department is required to advertise in accordance with the
  above-stated requirement.

  Bulletin Board and City Website – Formal Bids will be advertised by a notice posted

  the City’s solicitations.

  14
 2. Bid Terms and Conditions - This portion of the Bid Package contains a set of
  instructions and the general information needed to be considered by all bidders prior
  to bid submission. This information may include:

  a.  The term of the agreement
  b.  Tax exempt information
  c.  The rights of accepting or rejecting bids
  d.  Non-discrimination provisions
  e.  Standard shipping and delivery instructions
  f.  Payment terms
  g.  How to complete and submit the bid forms
  h.  Criteria to be used in evaluating the bid
  i.  Any other factors pertinent to that particular bid

3. Bid Security - The purpose of Bid Security is to ensure that: the bidders do not
  withdraw their bids within the period specified for acceptance; the bidders will honor
  the award of the bid as executed by the City; and that the bidders will provide bonds
  or insurance certifications required by the City. If required, Bid Security shall be
  indicated in the Bid Terms and Conditions, as well as in the Notice Inviting Bids.

  a. Bid Security may be presented in a number of acceptable forms: Cashier's check,
  certified check, money order, or bid bond signed by an admitted surety insurer (a
  surety company authorized to do business in California).

  b. The amount of the Bid Security should be at least 10 percent of the total bid, and
  may be increased, if deemed necessary by the City Attorney or Purchasing
  Authority (City Controller) or respective Department Director.

  c. The Bid Security should be returned to each unsuccessful bidder within 20 days
  after the successful bidder has signed the contract.

  d. The Bid Security must also be returned to the successful bidder. If the successful
  bidder refuses or fails to execute the contract within 5 days after the notice of the
  award of the contract has been mailed, the successful bidder shall forfeit the Bid
  Security, and the City Council may award the contract to the next lowest
  responsible bidder.

  e. Bidders who regularly do business with the City shall be permitted to file with the
  City Clerk an annual bid bond in an amount established by the Purchasing
  Authority. Such annual bonds shall be acceptable as surety in lieu of the furnishing
  of surety with each individual transaction. If required by law, a copy of such bond
  shall accompany the bid, and the annual bond shall afford sufficient security for
  the specific bid.

4. Performance Bond - The Purchasing Authority has authority to require a Performance
  Bond before entering into a contract. Such bond must be in an amount deemed
  reasonably necessary to protect the best interest of the City. If it is determined that a
  Performance Bond is to be posted prior to entering into a contract, the form and
  amount of the bond must be described in the public Notice Inviting Bids, as well as in
  the Bid Terms and Conditions. A Performance Bond must be issued by an admitted
  surety insurer.

 5. Bidder's List - This is a listing of potential vendors that are believed to possess the

  a. Specifications set forth the essential characteristics of the items being purchased

Protest Procedures

Right to protest during pre-bid period - Any actual or prospective bidder, offeror or
contractor who is aggrieved in connection with the solicitation or award of a contract may
protest to the Purchasing Authority, in writing, within ten (10) days before the bid opening
or within five days after the bid opening. (NMC 3.20.160)

Filing of protest – Protests shall be made in writing to Purchasing Authority, within ten
(10) calendar days before the schedule bid opening or within five (5) business days after
the bid opening. A protest filed after the tenth (10th) day shall not be considered. A protest
lodged after award by the City Council will not be considered. Protests shall also be made,
in writing, if required, to any other state or federal agency, from which the City receives
grant funds. (NMC 3.20.170)

 Filing of protest during post bid evaluation and post award period - Protests shall be
 made in writing to the Purchasing Authority, within five (5) working days of notification a
 proposal has been recommended for award by the City; or after a proposal has been
 awarded. (NMC 3.20.160)
 Subject of protest - Protesters may file a protest on any phase of the solicitation or award
 including, but not limited to, specifications, preparation, bid solicitation, award or
 disclosure of information marked confidential in the bid or offer. (NMC 3.20.180)
 Form - The protest shall include:

  •  name and address of the protestor;

  •  appropriate identification of the procurement, and if the contract has been
  awarded the bid number;

  •  statement of reasons for the protest;

  •  supporting exhibits, evidence or documents to substantiate any claims unless
  not available within the filing time, in which case the expected availability date
  shall be indicated. (NMC 3.20.190)

 Notification of City Attorney
 The Purchasing Authority shall submit a copy of the protest to the City’s Attorney within
 three (3) working days of receipt of written protest. (NMC 3.20.200)
 Requested information – time of filing - Any additional information requested by any of
  18
 the parties should be submitted within the time periods established by the requesting
source in order to expedite consideration of the protest. Failure of any party to comply
expeditiously with a request for information by the Purchasing Authority may result in
resolution of the protest without consideration of any information, which is untimely filed
pursuant to such request. (NMC 3.20.210)

Stay of procurements during protest – (NMC 3.20.220)
A. When a protest has been filed within the designated period and before an award has
  been made, the Purchasing Authority shall make no award of the contract until the
  protest has been settled and the City’s Attorney has advised to proceed with the
  award.
B. When a protest has been filed within the designated period after award has been
  made, the Purchasing Authority shall not proceed with finalizing the contract until the
  protest has been settled and the City’s Attorney has advised to proceed with the
  award.

C. The decision of the Purchasing Authority is appealable to the City Manager. If no
  appeal is filed within ten (10) calendar days in writing to the City Manager, the
  decision of the Purchasing Authority shall be final.
D. Should an appeal be received by the City Manager within the designated period, a
  response will be provided within five (5) working days and shall be considered final.
E. The City does reserve the right to proceed with the award of a proposal pending the
  resolution of a protest when it is determined by the City Manager that:
  i.  The items to be procured are urgently required;
  ii.  Delivery or performance will be unduly delayed by failure to make the
  award promptly; or
  iii.  Failure to make a prompt award will otherwise cause undue harm to the
  City or FTA funding requirements.

Making information on protests available
The Purchasing Authority shall provide information to any interested party only when
advised by the City’s Attorney to do so. (NMC 3.20.230)

Time for decisions
A decision on a protest shall be made by the Purchasing Authority as expeditiously as
possible after receiving all relevant, requested information, and only when advised by
the City’s Attorney to do so. (NMC 3.20.240)

Bid preparation costs
The City Attorney shall determine the extent of the costs to be incurred in connection with
the solicitation, including bid preparation costs other than attorney’s fees, when a protest
is sustained and the protesting bidder or offer or should have been but was not awarded

CHAPTER 3.17

Adoption of Uniform Public Construction Cost Accounting Act

The City has elected to be subject to the Uniform Public Construction Cost Accounting
Act (hereinafter referred to as the "CUPCCAA"). City contracts for Public Projects and
maintenance work shall be governed by applicable state laws including the CUPCCAA,
Public Contract Code Section 22000 et seq, and the California Uniform Construction Cost
Accounting Commission's (hereinafter, "UCAA Commission") policies and procedures
manual and cost accounting review procedures, as amended from time to time.”

Definitions

Unless the context otherwise requires, the following definitions, as well as the definitions
in Chapter 3.16 (Purchasing System), shall govern the construction of this chapter:

“Facility” means any plant, building, structure, ground facility, utility system, subject to
the limitation found in paragraph 3 of the “Public Project” definition below, real property,
streets and highways, or other public work improvement.

“Level 1 projects” means Public Projects below $60,000 the monetary threshold of
subdivision (a) of Section 22032 of the Public Contract Code. This project can be
performed by the employees of a public agency by force account, by negotiated contract,
or by purchase order.

“Level 2 projects" means Public Projects below the $200,000 monetary threshold of
subdivision (b) of Section 22032 of the Public Contract Code, may be let to contract by
informal procedures as set forth in this article

"Level 3 projects" means Public Projects of $200,000 or more, the monetary threshold
of subdivision (c) of Section 22032 of the Public Contract Code, except as otherwise
provided in this article, be let to contract by formal bidding procedure.

  “Public Project” means any of the following:

  a. Construction, reconstruction, erection, alteration, renovation, improvement,
  demolition and repair work involving any publicly owned, leased or
  operated facility;

  b. Painting or repainting of any publicly owned, leased or operated facility;

   c. In the case of a publicly owned utility system, “public property” includes
  only the construction, erection, improvement or repair of dams, reservoirs,
  power plants and electrical transmission lines of two hundred thirty
  thousand (230,000) volts and higher.

“Public Project” does not include maintenance work. For purposes of this article,
“maintenance work” includes all of the following:

  a. Routine, recurring and usual work for the preservation or protection of any
  publicly owned or publicly operated facility for its intended purposes;

  b. Minor repainting;

  c. Resurfacing of streets and highways at less than one inch;

  d. Landscape maintenance, including mowing, watering, trimming, pruning,
  planting, replacement of plants and servicing of irrigation and sprinkler
  systems;

  e. Work performed to keep, operate and maintain publicly owned water,

EMERGENCY PURCHASES

Local Emergency

In the event of the proclamation of a State or local emergency by the Governor or the
Director of Emergency Services, or the existence of a state of war emergency, the
Director of Emergency Services is empowered to obtain from other sources vital
supplies, equipment, and such other properties found lacking and needed for the
protection of life and property and to bind the City for the fair value thereof as provided
in Sections 3.16.070(C) and 3.16.150 and, if required immediately, to commandeer the
same for public use.

Emergency purchases (non Public Works)

Purchases made in order to protect the health, welfare or safety of the community.
  a. Emergency purchases must be cleared by the Purchasing Authority and will
  receive a purchase order number. This number must be given to the vendor for
  use on the packing slip or invoice.

  b. If the Finance Department is closed and an emergency purchase has to be made,
  the Department must inform the Finance Department as soon as possible after it
  happens. A purchase order number will be assigned and the vendor notified of
  the number.

  c. The City Manager or designee shall provide a full report on the emergency and
  work performed at the next meeting of the City Council, at which time the City
  Council must confirm such action by a four-fifths vote, and further determine
  appropriate action such as, but not limited to, whether work should continue
  without the benefit of informal or formal bidding.

Emergency purchases Public Works

In emergency situations, the competitive bidding procedure does not have to be
observed if requirements of Sections 20168 and 22050 of the Public Contract Code are
met. To ensure that all legal requirements are satisfied, the project manager must review
pertinent provisions of the Public Contract Code and consult the City Attorney. Key
provisions are as follows:
  26
   a. In the case of an emergency, the City Council may pass a resolution by a four-
  fifths vote declaring that the public interest and necessity demand the immediate
  expenditure of public funds to safeguard life, health, or property.

  b. Upon adoption of the resolution, the Council may expend any sum required in the
  emergency to repair or replace a public facility, take any directly related and
  immediate action required by that emergency, and procure the necessary
  equipment, services, and supplies, without giving notice for bids to let contracts.

  c. Before taking any action, the Council must make a finding, based on substantial
  evidence set forth in the minutes of its meeting, that the emergency will not permit
  a delay resulting from a competitive solicitation for bids, and that the action is
  necessary to respond to the emergency.

  d. The Council, by a four-fifths vote, may delegate, by resolution or ordinance, to the
  City Manager, City Engineer, or other non-elected officer, the authority to order
  any action.

  e. If a person with authority orders any action, that person must report to the Council,
  at its next meeting, the reasons justifying why the emergency will not permit a delay
  resulting from a competitive solicitation for bids and why the action is necessary to
  respond to the emergency.

  f. If the Council orders any action, it must review the emergency action at its next
  regularly scheduled meeting and at every regularly scheduled meeting thereafter
  until the action is terminated, to determine, by a four-fifths vote, that there is a need
  to continue the action.

  g. If a person with authority orders any action, the Council must initially review the
  emergency action not later than seven days after the action, or at its next regularly
  scheduled meeting if that meeting will occur not later than 14 days after the action,
  and at least at every regularly scheduled meeting thereafter until the action is
  terminated, to determine, by a four-fifths vote, that there is a need to continue the
  action, unless a person with authority has terminated that action prior to the Council
  reviewing the emergency action and making a determination.

  h. When the Council reviews the emergency action, it must terminate the action at
  the earliest possible date that conditions warrant so that the remainder of the
  emergency action may be completed by giving notice for bids to let contracts.

 SUSTAINABLE PURCHASING POLICY & PROCEDURES

The purpose of the Sustainable Purchasing Policy is to implement the City’s goals of
reducing greenhouse gas emissions and impacts on climate change, and generally
encouraging the City’s use of environmentally friendly and sustainably produced products
and services. Unless otherwise stated, the policies set forth in this section are aspirational
and should be adhered to whenever commercially reasonable. All definitions included in
this Section, unless otherwise provided for herein, shall have the definitions as provided
for under Section 8.50.030 of the Norwalk Municipal Code.

Life Cycle and Recyclability
  A. Use life cycle cost analysis to assist in selecting a product or service. The City
  should also consider the sustainability, circularity or recyclability of a product, and
  the percentage of recyclable content of the product in its analysis.

Carbon Emissions and Shipping
  A. Orders should be combined into as few shipments as possible to reduce emissions
  and waste from packaging and consider local City distribution points.
  B. Personnel should try to avoid shipping by air freight whenever possible.
  C. If available, orders should be placed with companies or delivery and distribution
  services that utilize electric, hybrid, or other low-emission delivery vehicles when
  practicable.
  D. Unless expressly prohibited for use in certain vehicles, including but not limited to
  any specifications required by the manufacturer, the purchase of lubricating oil and
  industrial oil from the seller whose oil product contains the greater percentage of
  recycled oil, if the availability, fitness, quality, and price of the recycled oil product
  is otherwise equal to, or better than, virgin oil products, in accordance with
  California Public Contract Code 10409.

Water Conservation
  A. When procuring products or services related to landscaping or other areas where
  water conservation measures could be implemented, personnel should consider
  the Landscape Standards and the Water Efficient Landscape Ordinance under
  NMC Section 17.03, Art. I.

Toxicity
  A. When purchasing products such as cleaning solutions, pesticides, and herbicides,
  purchases should attempt to purchase fewer and less toxic products whenever
  possible.
  B. Avoid the purchase of products containing persistent, bioaccumulative, or toxic
  chemicals that do not degrade or may accumulate within the human body,
  whenever practicable.

  A. Purchases of appliances should include energy-conserving and/or ENERGY
  STAR certified products whenever possible.

 CITY OF NORWALK PURCHASING CARD PROGRAM POLICY, PROCEDURES,
AND CARDHOLDER INSTRUCTIONS

BACKGROUND
The City uses a variety of methods to procure goods and services, but relies to a large
extent on the standard purchase order process - an essential financial control which
works very well for large purchases, but not as well for day-to-day needs.

To facilitate these small dollar day-to-day purchases, the City of Norwalk has entered
into a purchasing card agreement with US Bank. The City’s program is based upon the
State of California’s “Cal-Card” Purchasing Card Program. The purchasing card program
is designed to provide a fast, safe, and cost-effective purchasing method. It reduces the
need for purchase orders and increases the documentation and tracking of purchases
while encouraging more vendors to trade with the City.

Purchasing cards are assigned to selected employees who need to purchase supplies
and services in the course of their duties. A number of unique controls have been
developed for this program, controls that do not exist for traditional credit cards. These
controls ensure that the purchasing card can be used only for specific purposes and
within specific dollar limits. Cardholders are required to certify each purchase and a City
official verifies the appropriateness of each purchase.

PURPOSE
The purpose of this document is to establish guidelines for the issuance and use of
purchasing cards and to accomplish the following:

  1. To improve efficiency by reducing the need for small dollar purchase orders.

  2. To establish appropriate internal controls.

  3. To ensure that all purchases made with the cards conform to the City's purchasing
  ordinances and policies.

  4. To ensure that the City bears no legal liability from inappropriate use of purchasing
  cards.

GENERAL INFORMATION and DEFINITIONS
The City’s purchasing card program conforms to and operates jointly with the bank’s
purchasing card program. The responsibilities of the two entities and the responsibilities
of the cardholders are outlined below.

  1. Bank - The Bank issues the purchasing cards, monitors the system to verify that
  purchases fall within parameters established by the City, and provides monthly
  billing reports and other billing information as needed.

  2. The Purchasing Card - The purchasing card contains the individual employee's
  name, the City's name, the card account number, and an expiration date.

  3. Purchasing Agent - The Purchasing Agent has overall responsibility for the
  program. He or she is the overall program administrator and bank liaison,
  38
   responsible for accumulating, reporting, and coordinating all information to the
  participants, and to the City Council.

  4. Finance Department Staff - The Finance Staff verifies that each cardholder submits
  appropriate documentation including authorization of Approving Official in a timely
  manner. Account codes are reviewed for accuracy and monthly statements are
  paid.

  5. Approving Official - The Approving Official is responsible for reviewing the charges
  made by employees within his/her department or unit to ensure that all purchases
  made by cardholders in his/her area are appropriate, comply with applicable
  policies, and are properly documented. Ultimately, the City Manager, Department
  Directors and Division Managers are deemed Responsible Officials for the
  purposes of this program.

  6. Cardholder - The cardholder is the employee whose name is imprinted on the card.
  He or she is responsible for ensuring the card is used appropriately.

CONTROLS
A number of unique controls have been developed for this program that do not exist for
traditional credit cards.

  1. The purchasing card will have both the employee’s name and the City of Norwalk’s
  name imprinted on it.

  2. Cardholder Only - No one but the cardholder may use the card.

  3. Special Design – The card has been designed to avoid confusing it with the
  cardholder’s personal credit card. In all other respects, it is considered a regular
  credit card.

  4. Specific Purposes and Amounts – Guidelines have been established to ensure that
  the purchasing card can be used only for specific purposes and within specific
  dollar limits.

  5. Certification - Cardholders are required to review the monthly statements and
  certify each purchase as proper and appropriate.

  6. Supervisory Verification – The Approving Official for the cardholder verifies the
  appropriateness of each purchase.

  7. Management Oversight - The Purchasing Agent is responsible for the overall
  administration of the City’s purchasing card program. However, the Approving
  Official, as well as Department Directors performs key oversight and supervisory
  functions.

DISCIPLINE
  1. Any employee who uses the card in an improper or illegal manner is subject to
  discipline up to and including termination.

  2. Any employee who uses the card in violation of a law may be criminally prosecuted.

  39
 CARDHOLDER SPENDING LIMITS
Spending limits may vary, depending upon the duties and types of purchases required
of the employee.

  1. Individual Card Limits – Single purchase limits and monthly purchase limits have
  been established. Each time a cardholder uses his or her card to make a purchase,
  these limits are automatically checked. Authorization is denied if the purchase
  amount exceeds the limits.

  2. General Limits - the City's limits for purchasing cards are as follows:

  a. Single Purchase Limit:  $1,000

  b. 30-Day Total Limit:  $8,700

  3. Limits - A cardholder’s purchasing limits will be increased or lowered at the
  direction of the Approving Official, Department Director or City Manager.

  4. Cancellation - A card will be cancelled at the direction of the Approving Official,
  Department Director or City Manager.

CARD RESTRICTIONS
 1. Mixed Items - A single purchase may be comprised of many items, but the total
  cannot exceed the authorized single invoice limit allowed.

  2. Back Orders - All items purchased over-the-counter with a purchasing card must
  be immediately available. No back ordering is allowed.

  3. Cash Advances – Cash advances are NOT permitted, whether through bank
  tellers, teller machines, or any other method.

  4. Personal Items – The purchase of personal items is NOT allowed.

  5. Services or Labor of any type – All services or labor requires the prior approval of
  the Purchasing Agent to ensure that City insurance requirements are followed.

  6. Uniform – Any and all uniform-related purchases are not allowed on a City Cal-
  Card. These purchases should be paid as part of regular warrant payments
  through accounts payable.

  7. Software/Computer Equipment – No purchases of software, reoccurring charges
  for online services, or computer equipment/accessories are allowed on a City Cal-
  Card. Such charges should be paid as part of regular warrant payments through
  accounts payable, or made by the Finance Department on behalf of the requesting
  department.

  8. Fixed or Inventory Controlled Assets – Purchase of a fixed or inventory controlled
  assets requires the prior approval of the Purchasing Agent if over $500.

  40
   9. Travel – The purchase of airfare, registration costs, and lodging only are permitted.
  Parking/shuttle/transportation network company expenses are allowable if cash
  payment is not accepted. These travel expenses must be reported on page 2 of
  the Travel expense claim form. All other travel-related expenses are not allowed.

  10. Orders placed online through Amazon must use the City’s Amazon Business
  account – see - Procedures for Ordering Goods through Amazon for details.

  11. Alcoholic Beverages – No purchase of alcoholic beverages is allowed.

  12. Food – The purchase of food on a City Cal-Card is not permitted unless it is made
  to support a City program/event. When such purchases are made with a Cal-Card,
  a Cal-Card Confirmation Form must be completed and provided to the Finance
  Department.

  The purchase of food on a City Cal-Card while traveling is strictly prohibited and
  may result in the revoking of a Cal-Card.

  13. Fuel/Electric Charging – Purchases of gasoline and/or electric charging for both
  City and personal vehicles is not allowed.

  14. Gift Cards/Employee Recognition Items – The purchase of gift cards for employee
  recognition and/or other incentive items on a City Cal-Card is strictly prohibited.
  The aforementioned purchases must be submitted to, and approved by, the
  Human Resources Department. Once approved, only the Finance department is
  allowed to make such purchases on behalf of a requesting department.

  Gift cards may be paid with City Cal-Card if they are purchased to support a City
  program/event for the community. When such purchases are made with a Cal-
  Card, a Cal-Card Confirmation Form must be completed and provided to the
  Finance Department.

  15. Inappropriate Use Of City Funds – The purchase of any product or service normally
  considered to be an inappropriate use of City funds is NOT allowed.

  16. Additional limitations – Any Department participating in this program may add
  regulations and restrictions to this list for its employees. When such regulations
  and restrictions are implemented, the Finance Department must be notified to
  support said regulations and restrictions.

EXCEPTIONS
In order to maintain controls and provide flexibility to departments as needed, the
following exceptions apply:

  1. Finance Authority – The Finance Department may from time to time be exempt
  from the aforementioned card restrictions when the need for the purchase is
  deemed necessary and the restriction could result in a disruption to City
  operations. Departments needing to make purchases that fall within the card
  restrictions should consult with, and make a request to, the Finance Department
  to determine the need and make the transaction on the department’s behalf.

  No other department is exempt from such restrictions, unless it is approved by the
  41
   City Manager.

  2. Emergencies – Purchases made on a Cal-Card for emergencies are permissible
  so long as the purchase is within the transaction limits of the user. All purchases
  made for emergencies require a report to the City Council at the next available City
  Council Agenda.

ACQUIRING THE PURCHASING CARD
 1. Acquiring The Purchasing Card - To start the process, send a "Request for
  Purchasing Card" form to the Finance Department through the department’s
  Approving Official. Upon receipt, the Purchasing Agent will review the request, add
  the employee’s name to the program, and forward a request for a card to the bank.

  2. Training - It is mandatory that employees attend training on the proper use of the
  card and the monthly reporting of all program transactions.

  3. Personal Signature/Acknowledgement - After employees have successfully
  completed the training program, the Finance Department will provide the card, and
  the employee will be required to sign an acknowledgement that they understand
  and agree to comply with the laws, rules and regulations governing its use.

  4. Forms - Forms have been developed for use in the program. These forms are
  located on the shared citywide drive (W:\), in the Forms folder (Purchasing Card
  Program sub-folder). The following forms are included:
  a.  Request for City Purchase Card
  b.  Cardholder Statement of Questioned (Disputed) Item
  c.  Purchasing Card Issuance and Acknowledgement
  d.  Cal-Card Confirmation Form (when food, gift cards, etc. are purchased)

ACTIVATING THE CARD
Activate the card by removing the CCRV (Credit Card Receipt Verification) strip. Call the
phone number and follow the prompts. Instructions are included with your card.
Cardholder must register of online access on the US bank website.

USING THE PURCHASING CARD
The purchasing card is used like any other credit card, but it does not affect the user’s
personal credit rating or personal accounts. This is strictly a business card and the
merchants accepting the card are engaging in City business.

  1. Any Merchant – Employees may use their card at any business that accepts credit
  cards unless specified otherwise in this policy.

  2. Credit Card Payment Slip – The payment slip should include the following
  information:
  a. The merchant’s name, address and identification number.
  b. The last 4 digits of the account number, the expiration date, and the
  employee’s name.
  c. The date and the amount of the purchase,
  d. Itemized description of item(s) purchased - not all vendors will provide this
  information.
  e. Online/telephone transaction may provide email confirmation with the
  information listed above.
  42
   3. Signature - The merchant will request the cardholder to sign the merchant copy of
  the credit card payment slip. Verify that the dollar amount is correct and that sales
  tax has been included.

  4. Proof Of Purchase – The cardholder will be provided with the customer copy of the
  credit card payment slip, which should be kept in the Monthly Receipt Envelope. If
  the credit card payment slip does not have itemized information, obtain this
  information from the vendor. Cardholders will need itemized purchase receipts to
  verify the charges listed on the monthly statement of account.

  5. Prepare for Month-End Report - After using the purchasing card, the cardholder
  must prepare for the required month-end reporting process. Receipt envelopes
  have been provided for this purpose.

  6. Organization - All receipts and other documents associated with the use of the
  card must be placed in the envelope for reconciliation with the month-end bank
  statement.

  7. Forward the Package - Upon verification of the charges for the month, forward the
  entire package to the department Approving Official for approval of payment, once
  approved, the package should be sent directly to the Finance Department.

  8. Security – The cardholders responsibility for the proper use of a purchasing card
  includes, of course, the proper accounting of its use. Keep receipt envelopes in a
  safe, secure place.

DOCUMENTATION
 1. Proof Of Purchase - Any time a purchase is made using the card, a receipt
  itemizing each item purchased along with the credit card payment information must
  be retained as proof of purchase.

  2. Missing Receipts - In the event a cardholder has misplaced or is not in possession
  of a receipt, a memo can be submitted in lieu of receipts. The memo must state
  the purchase, itemizing the amount when needed, and signed by the department
  head. If an employee misplaces more than three receipts during a fiscal year, the
  Cal-card will be revoked.

  3. Shipping Documents - Shipping documents will be attached to proof of purchase,
  if available.

BOOKKEEPING, RECONCILLIATION, AND PAYMENT PROCEDURES

INDIVDUAL CARD HOLDERS
Each month, each cardholder will have to download the bank statement from the US
Bank website, verify the correctness of the charges it contains, attach the receipts, and
forward the package to your Approving Official.

  1. Statement of Account – Billing cycle closes each month on the 23rd day.
  Statements need to be download by each cardholder. The statement will itemize
  each transaction charged to your purchasing card. The following information must
  be provided:
  43
   a. Account Codes - Insert the account code for each transaction on the
  statement.
  b. Documentation - Verify that there is an itemized sales receipts and packing
  slips (if available) for each charge listed on the statement of account.
  c. Any billing errors or adjustments should be noted on the statement of
  account.

  2. Submit - The completed and verified statement and receipts must be submitted to
  the Approving Official, by the 26th of each month.
  a. The Approving Official must sign and submit the approved statement with
  documentation to the Finance Department by the last day of each reporting
  month.
  b. If the 23rd or the last day of the month falls on either a weekend or a dark
  Friday, statements are due to Approving Official on the following Monday.

  3. Credit Voucher - If an item is returned for credit, include the credit voucher with the
  statement on which the credit appears.

  4. Missing Documents – If, for some reason, the cardholder does not have
  documentation of the transaction to send with the statement, he/she must attach
  a memorandum explaining why there is no supporting documentation and include
  a description of the item, the date of purchase, and the merchant’s name. This is
  not to be used as a regular process to replace missing receipts. If more than three
  transaction documents are missing in a fiscal year, the Cal-card will be revoked.

  5. On-Leave - If an employee will not be available to sign a statement because of
  leave or travel, forward all sales receipts and credit vouchers to the department
  Approving Official. The Approving Official will sign and forward the envelope to the
  Finance Department. However, paperwork should be submitted prior to any leave
  for an extended period of time.

  6. Questioned Purchase - If the department Approving Official questions a purchase
  made with a purchasing card, the cardholder must be able to explain the nature of
  the purchase.

  a. Investigation - If the cardholder cannot substantiate the purchase was
  necessary and for official use, a department will investigate to determine
  improper use of the purchasing card.

  b. Disciplinary Action - Any resulting disciplinary action is handled directly by
  a Department Director.

PAYMENT AND INVOICE PROCEDURES
  1. Statement of Account - The bank will provide a summary statement of account to
  the Purchasing Agent and a copy to each cardholder at the end of the billing cycle.
  The statement of account will have a listing of all items processed in the previous
  thirty days.

  2. The summary statement of account will be reviewed by the Purchasing Agent and
  then submitted to Accounts Payable for payment, in order to maximize the amount
  of rebate received.
  44
   a. Questions regarding individual charges may be brought to the attention of
  card holders at this time.

3. Completed and verified individual cardholder statements will be returned to the
  Finance Department. These statements will be reviewed for completeness.

4. Cardholder Reconciliation - The cardholder reviews the statement of account for
  the following:

  a. Errors in Billing – make notes on the bill.

  b. Attach copies of all itemized receipts and credit card payment slips to
  his/her copy of the statement.

  c. Assign budget account codes to each item.

  d. Signs statement, certifying that the listed items were purchased for the City.

  e. Forwards the statement to the Approving Official not more than three
  working days from its receipt.

5. Review and Approval - The Approving Official is responsible the following:

  a. Review completed statements from all cardholders assigned to them.
  i. If statement is not received it is his/her responsibility to contact the
  cardholders and have the statements completed at once.

  b. Resolve any outstanding questions regarding purchases made by
  cardholders.

  c. Approving expenses by signing account statements.

  d. Forward completed statements of account with all documentation to the
  Finance Department within one working day after receipt from the
  cardholders.

6. Finance Staff will review each cardholders statement for the following:

  a. Verify that each item purchased complies with the City of Norwalk
  purchasing ordinance or its policies and procedures.

  b. Verify that sales tax was charged for items purchased- collect information
  for quarterly sales tax payment.

  c. Check purchases for items that may require Inventory control tags.

7. Finance Staff member will post all transactions to Funding Accounting after review
  is complete.

  45
 APPROVAL ISSUES
No policy statement can totally define all transaction approvals. The position of
Approving Official was created because the people assigned to the task have both the
supervisory responsibilities and knowledge of the cardholder’s job responsibilities to
understand what is and is not appropriate and to deal with issues that evolve. The
Approving Official must review each cardholder's purchases and the actions of the
merchant who made the sale, in order to determine if the items were for official use and
are allowed to be purchased within this program. If, for any reason, the Approving Official
questions a purchase, it is his/her responsibility to resolve the question with the
cardholder.

  1. Proof Of Return - If the Approving Official cannot be satisfied that a purchase was
  necessary and for official use, then the cardholder must provide a credit voucher
  proving that the items(s) were returned for credit.

  2. Investigation – It is the responsibility of the Approving Official to resolve questions
  regarding possible improper use of the purchasing card. If the cardholder cannot
  provide such credit voucher, the Approving Official must investigate the matter.

  3. Disciplinary Action – Whenever the Approving Official determines that an
  employee has used a purchasing card improperly, he or she will provide a written
  report to the Purchasing Agent explaining the situation and the conclusions he or
  she reached. The Purchasing Agent is responsible for notifying the Department
  Director and the City Manager and recommending disciplinary action for any
  misuse of the card.

  4. Theft Or Other Crime – If it is determined that the misuse of the card involved theft
  or any other crime, the Purchasing Agent will report the matter to the Sheriff’s
  Department.

DISPUTED TRANSACTIONS
In the course of day-to-day business, purchased items are not always satisfactory and
adjustments are occasionally needed. If any items purchased with the card are defective
or the repair and/or service is faulty, the cardholder is responsible for resolving the
problem with the merchant. If the merchant refuses to replace or correct the faulty item
or to give the cardholder credit for its return, then the purchase is considered to be in
dispute.

  1. Statement Of Questioned Items - A disputed item should be identified on the
  cardholder's Statement of account. A Statement of Questioned Items form must
  be completed by the cardholder and the appropriate documentation must be
  attached. This form shall be forwarded with the statement of account through the
  Approving Official to the Purchasing Agent for disposition by the bank. Once the
  bank has disposed of the matter, the Purchasing Agent will notify the cardholder
  and Approving Official of the action taken.

  2. Reconciliation - When a disputed charge appears on your statement, you must
  assign it a City budget account number, so it can be debited. Once the problem is
  resolved and a credit shows on your statement, assign it the same account number
  for credit. As long as a charge is shown on your statement with no offsetting credit,
  payment must be made.
  46
   3. Reversal Of Charges – Protect your right to dispute a charge. Reports of disputed
  items must be submitted within the 45-day period established by the bank.

  4. Help – For any questions regarding the information on the form, or for any
  problems regarding the reversal of a transaction, please contact the Finance
  Department.

LOST OR STOLEN CARDS
If your card is lost or stolen, immediately notify your Approving Official, the Finance
Department and the bank. In the case of a crime, such as robbery, burglary, or theft,
notify the police or Sheriff’s Department in the area where the crime occurred.

  1. Information To Report - Provide the following information to your Approving Official
  and the Purchasing Agent your complete name, card number, date reported to the
  police, if applicable, date and time the bank was notified, and any purchases made
  on the day the card was lost or stolen.

  2. Approving Official Report - The Approving Official must submit a written report to
  the Purchasing Agent within three working days of receiving such notification. The
  report should state the date the loss was discovered, the location where the theft
  or loss occurred, if known, and any other relevant information.

  3. New Card Issued - A new card is issued by the bank within five (5) business days
  from the time that you report the loss or theft. A new personal account number is
  assigned to your new card.

CHANGES
Employee status changes may require the cancellation of an existing card and the
issuance of a new card.

  1. New Name, Address, Department - Changes to your name, address, or
  Department/Division may result in the cancellation of your card. A new card may
  need to be issued. The cardholder is responsible for reporting the change and
  submitting the new application.

  2. Leaving City Employment: - Your authority to use the card is automatically
  cancelled upon leaving City employment.

  a. Final Paperwork - Submit your completed envelope and purchasing card to
  your.

  b. Approving Official. The Approving Official is responsible for turning it in the
  packet and card to the Purchasing Agent.

  a. Don’t Use It - If you fail to turn in your purchasing card upon leaving City
  employment, do not purchase with it. Any charges made after your
  termination date or following the last date you were authorized to make a
  purchase for the City will not be honored and you will be responsible for the
  charges.

  b. Card not retrieved - If the Approving Official is not able to retrieve the card
  47
   before a cardholder leaves the City, he or she must immediately notify the
  Purchasing Agent so they can immediately contact the bank and void the
  card.

INVENTORY
The Purchasing Agent may request a physical inventory of the cards at any time. The
Approving Official will verify the cards and report the results to the Purchasing Agent.

On March 28, 2024, the City issued an Invitation for Bid (IFB) No. 24-763 for Cummins Original
Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) Parts and Minor Repair Services for Norwalk Transit System
(NTS). The purpose of the IFB is to acquire Cummins OEM parts and repair services for the
NTS fleet that includes and an aging Compressed Natural Gas Fleet and first generation of Zero
Emissions Buses (ZEBs) that are no longer under warranty.

NTS received three (3) bids including 1) Cummins, Inc., 2) Harbor Diesel & Equipment, Inc., 3)
Rush Truck Centers of California, Inc. Staff reviewed the bids and determined that Cummins, Inc.
provided the lowest and most responsive/responsible bid.

contract totals $70,000 which is included in the Fiscal Year 2024/25 Transportation Department
adopted budget. There is no impact to the general fund.

SUBJECT:  PROJECT NO. 7872 - RESOLUTION NO. 24-33 - BUDGET AMENDMENT -

  SERVICES PARKING LOT RESURFACING

Background:

On April 25, 2024, City Staff solicited a Notice Inviting Bids for Project No. 7872, Transportation
Center and Social Services Parking Lot Resurfacing (Project). The Project will rehabilitate
parking lots for the City’s shared Transportation Center, and the Social Services Center and
Alondra Library. The scope of work includes for pavement surface preparation, specific location
pavement repairs, pavement resurfacing, and pavement markings restoration.

The City held two pre-bid meetings which included site visits for both project locations. Five
contractors attended the first pre-bid meeting held on May 2, 2024. Two contractors attended
the second pre-bid meeting held on May 13, 2024. Bids were due on May 20, 2024, at 10 a.m.
Two Bids were received in response to this solicitation.

All American Asphalt:  $395,021
MAJ Engineering:  $278,983

City staff reviewed bids for accuracy, costs, contractor experience, work on similar projects, and
references. The bid submitted by MAJ Engineering was non-responsive. All American Asphalt
was the lowest responsible and responsive bid for the Project. As a result, staff recommends
awarding the project contract to All American Asphalt of Corona California based on their bid
and qualifications. All American Asphalt has recently completed similar projects within the City
and nearby cities like Monterey Park, Loma Linda and Ontario.

  FUNDS

Background:

On April 28, 2017, the Governor signed Senate Bill 1 (SB1), also known as the Road Repair and
Accountability Act of 2017. The objective of SB1 is to address deferred maintenance on local
street and road systems through the prioritization and delivery of basic road maintenance and
rehabilitation projects as well as critical safety projects.

SB1 created the Road Maintenance and Rehabilitation Account (RMRA), to be funded and
apportioned to cities based on gas and diesel fuel excise tax, vehicle registration, and the
California Consumer Price Index. The exact amount that the City receives will vary
annually. Below is a list of the funds received to date and Fiscal Year (FY) estimates:

  FISCAL YEAR  SB1 FUNDS
  FY 2020/21  $1,985,094  Actual
  FY 2021/22  $2,138,601  Actual
  FY 2022/23  $2,204,304  Actual

  FY 2023/24  $2,475,950  Actual
  FY 2024/25  $2,646,659 Estimated
 City Council  June 18, 2024
Resolution No. 24-36 – Adoption of List of Projects for  Page No. 2
Fiscal Year 2024/25 RMRA Funds

On March 24, 2021, the California Transportation Commission (CTC) adopted revised guidelines
for RMRA funds. The guidelines state that eligible RMRA activities include but are not limited
to: road maintenance and rehabilitation, safety projects, complete streets components, traffic
control devices, and satisfaction of match requirements.

The guidelines also state that cities must submit a City Council approved proposed project list
to the CTC. Below is a brief overview of activities in processing applications of RMRA funds and
its associated dates:

Nos. 7920,7934,7935, and Independent Streets and Alleys will resurface approximately 20 miles
of residential and arterial streets funded by RMRA funds. The work is estimated to be complete
in FY 2024/25.

Staff evaluated the various needs of the City that are eligible under SB1 funding. Street
improvements were prioritized, followed by equipment purchases that can be utilized to maintain
the traffic signal infrastructure. Exhibit A of Resolution No. 24-36 lists the various uses of
FY 2024/25 RMRA funds accompanied by a location map (Attachment No.2) for City Council’s
consideration. The list can be edited as needed throughout the year via City Council resolution.
