  WHEREAS, Senate Bill 1 (SB 1), the Road Repair and Accountability Act of 2017
  (Chapter 5, Statutes of 2017) was passed by the Legislature and Signed into law by the
  Governor in April 2017 to address the significant multi-modal transportation funding
  shortfalls statewide;

  WHEREAS, SB 1 includes accountability and transparency provisions that will
  ensure the residents of our City are aware of the projects proposed for funding in our
  community and which projects have been completed each fiscal year;

  WHEREAS, the City of Norwalk must adopt by resolution a list of projects
  proposed to receive fiscal year funding from the Road Maintenance and Rehabilitation
  Account (RMRA), created by SB 1, which must include a description and the location of
  each proposed project, a proposed schedule for the project’s completion, and the
  estimated useful life of the improvement; and

  WHEREAS, the City of Norwalk will receive an estimated $2,646,659 in RMRA
  funding in Fiscal Year 2024/25 from SB 1; and

  WHEREAS, this is the eighth year in which the City of Norwalk is receiving SB 1
  funding and will enable the City to continue essential road maintenance and rehabilitation
  projects, safety improvements, repairing and replacing aging bridges, and increasing
  access and mobility options for the traveling public that would not have otherwise been
  possible without SB 1; and

  WHEREAS, the City has undergone a robust public process to ensure public input
  into our community’s transportation priorities and project list through community forums,
  publication of upcoming street work in the Norwalk Now newsletter, and opportunity to
  give public comment at each City Council meeting; and

  WHEREAS, the City used a Pavement Management System to develop the SB 1
  project list to ensure revenues are being used on the most high-priority and cost-effective
  projects that also meet the communities priorities for transportation investment, with CIP
  No.7920, 7934, 7935, and Independent Streets and Alleys having streets with very poor
  rating (PCI 11-25) from the 2020 Pavement Management Study conducted by Bucknam
  Infrastructure Group, Inc.; and

  approximately nineteen and three quarter miles residential street pavement segments
  with a grind and overlay treatment and/or AR cape seal w/ type II slurry, this Fiscal Year

   WHEREAS, the City desires to mitigate and maintain safe passage upon

its efforts of maintenance to prolong and maximize street pavement service life; and

SUBJECT:  PROJECT NOS. 7869 AND 7870 - PHASE I ENERGY PROJECT -
  RESOLUTION NO. 24-37 – BUDGET AMENDMENT

Background:

The City’s Strategic Plan outlines the City’s commitment to sustainability and climate resistance.
To do so, staff worked with Syserco Energy Solutions (“SES”), a qualified energy services
company, to develop an analysis of opportunities for the City to upgrade its facilities to achieve
energy efficiency and cost savings measures.

On November 7, 2023, City Council adopted Resolution No. 23-68 authorizing the City Manager
to finalize negotiations with SES and acquire the necessary conservation equipment to
implement the energy conservation measures through the Sustainability, Energy Efficiency
Infrastructure Improvement Project, (Project).

Analysis

The Project was divided by component, which includes various energy saving measures, such
as Lighting, Solar, and heating, ventilation, and air conditioning control (HVAC). Phase I of the
project consists of the HVAC and Sports Lighting components of the project. To begin work, and
track expenditures by component accurately, the City established project numbers for each
component of the overall project. A summary of the project numbers assigned to each
component of Phase I is detailed in Table 1 on the following page.

  panels at Sports Complex, Aquatic Pavilion and Well 10 facilities.

SUBJECT:  AGREEMENT AMENDMENT NO. 3 FOR ON-CALL COMMUNITY

Background:

On November 7, 2023, City Council approved an agreement with The Code Group, Inc. (VCA)
to provide on-call Community Development Consultant and Additional Services intended to
support Community Development and other City departments with staff augmentation services,
priority projects, long-range planning projects, technical review and preparation for
environmental review documents. The agreement was approved for an amount not-to-exceed
$150,000 annually for a three-year term and ends October 2026.

Amendment No. 1 increased the maximum compensation amount of the contract to $150,000
annually as approved. The contract with VCA currently helps offset staff shortages in the Building
and Planning Divisions. Community Development Department (Department) has used the
following services since the contract was executed: Building Inspection Services, Building
Official Services, Senior Permit Techician Services, and Planning Manager Services. The
Department is working closely with the Human Resources Department to recruit for the vacant
positions and has multiple recruitments underway. On June 4, 2024, City Council approved
Amendment No. 2 increasing the maximum compensation amount of the contract to $375,000
through October 25, 2024.

VCA and their consultants submitted a proposal for design services for the Security & Safety
Improvements and Emergency Operations Center (EOC) Bathroom Upgrades Projects. The
project includes architectural and engineering design services for the project areas. The project
will create a secure entryway into City Hall; re-configuring the current entrance to accommodate
a greeter counter and additional office space for Public Safety staff. The adjacent office area
in Room 15 will be converted to office space for Community Development and Public Affairs
staff. Additionally, the EOC restrooms in the lower level of City Hall will be remodeled and

SUBJECT:  AGREEMENT FOR SENIOR NUTRITION PROGRAM, FISCAL YEAR 2024/25

Background:

The City has had an agreement with the Los Angeles (LA) County Aging and Disabilities
Department for the past five years, to provide nutritious meals to the senior community. In 2023,
the City partnered with Trio Community Meals, LLC (TCM), for catering services. They are one
of the several caterers the LA County permits the City to use. The cost for each individual meal
is competitive with most caterers. TCM are quick to respond to any questions or adjustments
requested by staff. The quality of the meals has dramatically increased attendance for
congregate meals and is regularly acknowledged by the patrons. It is in the best interest of the
Senior Nutrition Program to renew TCM’s services for Fiscal Year 2024/25.

Fiscal Impact:

Funds in the amount of $630,000 will be allocated towards the payment of services. These funds
will be reimbursed through the LA County Aging and Disabilities Department Grant Elder
Nutrition Program 242507.

Citizens Advised:

N/A

Strategic Plan 2023 Implementation:

The recommended action will further the City’s Strategic Plan Goal 1. Provide High Quality
Customer Service to the Community. Objective 1. Promote customer-focused culture that prizes
accessible, consistent, and predictable delivery of service.

Staff recommends City Council approve an agreement with Trio Community Meals, LLC, in the

execute the agreement and any amendments provided there is funding in the budget and it is
within the City Manager’s signing authority, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City
Attorney.

SUBJECT:  AGREEMENT AMENDMENT NO. 2 - EMERGENCY STREET LIGHT
  MAINTENANCE SERVICE PROVIDERS AND STREET LIGHT POLE
  REPLACEMENTS

Background:

In August 2018, the City took ownership of 3,333 existing street light poles citywide that were
purchased from Southern California Edison. In September 2019, the City advertised for
emergency on-call street light repair, replacement, and maintenance services. Services included
but not limited to are: repairs for street light pole knockdowns, exposed or damaged electrical
components and wiring, damaged traffic signal cabinets, vandalism and copper wire theft and
services requiring an experienced traffic signal technician. The Contractor provides all
equipment, materials, vehicles, transportation, personnel, and licenses and certifications
necessary to complete the work.

Agreements are based on the contractor’s hourly labor and equipment rates for responding to
incidents during normal business hours versus after hours. A 12% mark-up is included for street
light poles purchased by the City, stored and installed by the contractor. The contractor will be
required to respond to any emergency knockdown within 45 minutes. On an annual basis, the
City budgets for these services, in addition to the costs for purchasing replacement street light
poles, street light fixtures and bulbs, and traffic signal and other related supplies and materials.

Due to the nature of emergency response services, and availability of contractors, staff
recommended entering into agreements with two contractors. If City staff are not able to reach
the primary contractor, or they are not able to respond within the timeline, the secondary
contractor is contacted. In October of 2019, City Council approved agreements with Siemens
Mobility Inc. of Riverside (now Yunex LLC “Yunex”) as the primary contractor and Computer
Service Company (now Crosstown Electrical and Data Inc. “Crosstown”) as the secondary

contractor for emergency on-call services. The initial agreement term was from the effective date
through June 30, 2021, with the option to extend for two additional one-year periods through
June 30, 2023. Services provided by Yunex and Crosstown have been essential with handling
of streetlight and traffic signal related repairs, replacements, and maintenance needs. Due to
this, term of their agreements were extended to June 30, 2024.

Extending the agreement terms for services with Yunex and Crosstown for fiscal year (FY)
2024/25 allows them to address the City’s current open work orders with existing street light
poles in stock and assist City staff with future emergencies that may arise.

For information, 27 street light poles have been damaged/knocked down and 18 of them have
been replaced to date.

Fiscal Impact:

Costs for these services will vary depending on the personnel and equipment needed, time spent
to complete the work, and pricing of street light poles and materials needed. Estimated
expenditures for both Yunex and Crosstown are included in the approved FY 2024/25 Public
Services General Fund budget in the amount of $515,000.

Background:

The City received the attached letter from the County of Los Angeles Chief Executive Office
requesting that the City Council, as governing body for the City of Norwalk and former Norwalk
South-East Recreation and Park District, adopt a Joint Tax Transfer Resolution (Resolution)
authorizing the negotiated exchange of property tax revenue between the County, the cities, and
the Downey Cemetery District, Little Lake Cemetery District, and Artesia Cemetery District.

The Resolution provides tables that specify the tax rate areas and their corresponding annual
tax increment ratios that will be transferred to each district for each fiscal year. The document
also mentions the annexation of territory and the filing of a statement of boundary change for
the Reorganization 2021-03 with the Board of Equalization. The area proposed for annexation
is identified as Reorganization 2021-03 to reorganize approximately 81± acres of inhabited
territory located in the Cities of Bell Gardens, Bellflower, Cerritos, Downey, La Mirada,
Lakewood, Norwalk, Paramount, Santa Fe Springs, South Gate; and Los Angeles County
unincorporated territory (South Whittier).

Section numbers 21, 34, 41 and 42 of the attached Resolution relate to the City of Norwalk as
Norwalk South-East Recreation and Park District (SERPD) and to the City of Norwalk. The
combined impact to the City’s property tax revenues is a loss of 0.002022501 in annual tax
increment ratio, to the Downey Cemetery District and Little Lake Cemetery District. The following
table summarizes the overall impact of each section.

TO:  Honorable City Council

FROM:  Jesus M. Gomez, City Manager

BY:  Rebecca Bridgeford, Senior Management Analyst

SUBJECT:  AGREEMENT  AMENDMENT  NO.  1  -  MANAGEMENT  INFORMATION
  SYSTEMS

Background:

The Management Information Systems (MIS) department plays a crucial role in City operations,
delivering essential services that support the City’s commitment to providing high-quality
services to the community. Since 2009, Knight Communications, Inc. has been the City's internal
IT support provider with the most resent contract executed in 2019 for a five-year term ending
June 30, 2024.

As this contract approaches expiration, Staff proposes a short-term extension to provide
continuity of service to the City. This extension will allow time to develop a new scope of IT
support services that aligns with current industry standards and the City's evolving needs.
Additionally, if a new vendor is selected, the extension will facilitate a smooth transition, ensuring
continuity of IT support services.

Fiscal Impact:

Funding for MIS services is included in the Fiscal Year 2024/25 Budget. The contract extension
will be on a month-to-month basis, as needed, at the current rate of $23,850 per month, with a
total not-to-exceed amount of $143,100.

Strategic Plan 2023 Implementation:

The recommended action will further the City’s Strategic Plan Goal 1.3 - Transform the City's

Recommended Action:

Staff recommends City Council approve Amendment No. 1, providing for a month-to-month
extension with Knight Communications, Inc. for Management Information Systems services up
to six months no later than December 31, 2024 and not to exceed a total of $143,100.

SUBJECT:  MANAGEMENT ASSISTANCE OF ENGINEERING DIVISION – AGREEMENT
  AMENDMENT NO. 4

Background:

The Engineering Division (ED) is currently experiencing a surge in activities which include
several new street projects funded with various funds such as Senate Bill (SB)1, Measure M and
R Bonds; numerous Federally funded Traffic Signal Improvement Projects; City Council priorities
such Firestone Bridge Widening Project, and multiple park improvements citywide. On
November 18, 2021, a Professional Services Agreement was awarded to Mario Mera Consulting
(consultant) to provide project management support and services for the ED augmenting
staff. On May 2, 2023, an Amendment to the agreement was approved to provide management
assistance of the ED through June 30, 2024.

To ensure continuous successful management of the ED, staff recommends an amendment to
the agreement with the consultant to continue to provide management assistance of the ED, and
all other terms of the agreement remain in effect through June 30, 2027. Consultant’s work shall
be under the direction of the Director of Public Services/City Engineer (Director).

The Consultant will continue to provide supervision assistance over the ED, and shall: provide
technical and functional assistance, including para-professional, technical, and assistance in
support of the ED; assist in the preparation, coordination, and management of the ED operating
and capital improvement budgets; assist in evaluation of needs for and developing plans and
schedules for long-range Public Services projects; assist in the development and implementation
of the City’s budget and Capital Improvement Program; may act as ED liaison (as needed) with
other governmental agencies assisting in the development, planning, design, and construction
administration of cooperatively funded projects and programs; and regularly provide
statuses/updates on a timely basis to the Director of Public Services/City Engineer to effect
proper decision-making.
 City Council  June 18, 2024

Engineering Division

Based on project scheduling (design, construction, and close out efforts), the required
management assistance of Engineering Division efforts, programs, and existing staff,
management/support services are anticipated to extend through June 30, 2025.

Fiscal Impact:

This amendment shall extend the contract through Fiscal Year (FY) 2024/25 for an additional
cost of $297,600, which is included in the FY 2024/25 budget.

SUBJECT:  ADVISORY BODY APPOINTMENTS

Background:

With the exception of the Planning Commission (which is commensurate with the appointing
Councilmember’s term) and five members of the Art in Public Places Commission (which is
established in the Norwalk Municipal Code), Advisory Body terms are for two years following a
City election. Advisory Body terms are from January 1, of odd years to December 31, of even
years.

There are vacancies on several Advisory Bodies: Art in Public Places (4), Historical Heritage
(4), Community Promotion (1), Public Safety (1), Senior Citizens (1), and the Youth Commission
(all 15). The Youth Commission does not have any members at this time. The age range for the
Youth Commission is between 13 to 18 years of age. Each City Councilmember has three
appointments.

Two of the vacancies on the Art in Public Places Committee are appointed based on Norwalk
Municipal Code §15.44.060, and require consensus of the entire City Council. Those positions
are: one at-large Community Representative and one Outside Authority with Expertise in Art.

SUBJECT:  PUBLIC HEARING - RESOLUTION NO. 24-35 - SETTING SEWER SERVICE
  CHARGE FOR FISCAL YEAR 2024/25 AND ORDERING THAT SUCH CHARGE
  BE COLLECTED ON THE TAX ROLL

Background:

On June 18, 2013, City Council adopted Ordinance No. 13-1642 establishing sewer
service charges to pay for the operation and maintenance of the City’s sewer system, including
capital replacement costs. Ordinance No. 13-1642 provided that beginning July 1, 2014, the
sewer service charge could be increased annually through July 1, 2018 by an amount equal to
the annual increase in the Engineering News Record Construction Cost Index for the Los
Angeles Area (the “ENRLA”), as of February of each year. The City has not increased the sewer
service charges since Fiscal Year 2017/18.

Norwalk Municipal Code (NMC), Chapter 13.14 and the California Health and Safety Code,
Article 4 of Chapter 6 of Part 3 of Division 5, Section 5470, affirms that City Council is authorized
to levy an annual sewer service charge and to have such charge collected on the property tax
roll.

As required by the California Health and Safety Code, each year that the City levies and collects
charges on the tax roll, the City must prepare a Sewer Service Charge Roll (Report) that contains
a description of each parcel of real property to which the charge is applicable and the amount of
the charge for each parcel and must hold a public hearing. The Report is available for public
inspection in City Clerk’s Department or may be viewed online on the City’s webpage. As
provided in the Report, the proposed charge for each parcel is the amount authorized by NMC
Chapter 13.14.020, Section E.
 City Council  June 18, 2024
Resolution No. 24-35 - Sewer Service Charge Fiscal Year 2024/25  Page No. 2

On November 21, 2017, City Council voted to continue to levy and collect the sewer service
charge with no increase each fiscal year until the City updates its 2015 Sewer Master Plan study
and conducts a new sewer service fee study. A Sewer System Management Plan update is
nearly complete, and Sewer Master Plan update is currently underway.

Attached Resolution No. 24-35 approves the Report and authorizes the levy of the charge on
the property tax roll for FY 2024/25 per Chapter 13.14 of the NMC. Adoption of the attached
resolution requires approval by two-thirds of the members of City Council.

Following is a list of projects that the City has recently completed, are in process, and/or
scheduled for the next few years using the sewer service fee revenues:

  •  Project No. 7519 – (90% complete) design and installation of a new Sewer System
  Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) system
  •  Project No. 7520 – (100% complete) design and upgrade of Bloomfield Sewer Lift Station
  Upgrade Project
  •  Project No. 7521 – (complete) repaired 57 point locations of sewer mainline under FY
  2017/18 Sewer Main Repair Project using various methods
  •  Project No. 7522 – (65% complete) evaluates 450 sewer manholes and repairs selected
  manholes per NASSCO MACP guidelines
  •  Project No. 7523 – (10% complete) design and improvement of 12 pipe segments of the
  sewer system (Phase 4)
  •  Project No. 7524 - (10% complete) evaluates 300-400 sewer manholes and repairs
  selected manholes per NASSCO MACP guidelines
  •  Project No. 7525 – (10% complete) design and improvement of 60 pipe segments of the
  sewer system (Phase 5 Project)
  •  Project No. 7527 – (40% complete) Force Main Replacements for two sewer lift stations

Fiscal Impact:

The annual fee revenue projected for FY 2024/25 is approximately $2,500,000. The actual
amount collected will not be known until after receiving the first installment payments.

SUBJECT:  ONE-WAYS NEIGHBORHOOD REHABILITATION PROGRAM SUMMARY

Background:

On July 19, 2022, City Council approved an allocation of $2,000,000 for the One-Ways
Neighborhood Rehabilitation Program (Program) to serve a community that has been
disproportionately impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic. In August of 2022, staff was hired to
develop and administer the Program.

Community outreach commenced in Fall 2022 to promote the Program to the residents in the
area. In February 2023, staff hosted three community meetings at the Norwalk Social Services
Center to provide program information and application assistance. From March 1-31, the
submission period opened to accept applications on a first-come first-serve basis to participate
in the Program. Following the end of the submission period, an evaluation committee conducted
an in-depth review of 85 applications that consisted of document review and field inspections.

A total of 80 applicants were approved and the following services have been completed:

  •  Roof Replacement: 56
  •  Exterior Paint: 14
  •  Fence Repair/Replacement: 9
  •  Junk Removal: 1

The One-Ways Neighborhood Rehabilitation Program has remaining funds of $175,000.

Staff will review the initial One-Ways surveys received to reach out to interested property owners
for potential rehabilitation assistance to use the remaining funds.
 City Council  June 18, 2024

Fiscal Impact:

A total of $2,000,000 in general funds has been allocated for the program and associated parking
study.
